Quick notes for the questionnaire answers (drafted below — will formalize in the doc):

- Hosted (Redwood API): default request/response payload logs are retained for 30 days. Operational/diagnostic logs (metrics, infra traces) are retained 90 days. Access logs (auth + routing) are retained 90 days by default. Backups (periodic full snapshots) are kept for 12 months and are immutable snapshots used only for DR.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): retention windows are configurable per-customer; typical defaults mirror hosted but can be reduced on request. Backups live on customer-dedicated storage; retention policy is set via the Dedicated deployment config.
- Private/on-prem: Redwood control plane is limited; retention and backups are customer-managed (we provide the tooling and recommended configs).
- Deletion SLA: for hosted deployments we aim to complete customer-initiated deletion requests within 30 business days for primary data. For backups/snapshots the propagation timeline is separate — snapshots are not immediately rewritten; we provide a documented process to scrub or rotate snapshots on request and can commit to removal within the backup retention period (we recommend surfacing a contractual language window of up to 90 days for full propagation depending on snapshot cadence).
- HIPAA/BAA: supported with Private deployments or Dedicated with a signed BAA. For Hosted we can support via contractual BAA in many cases; legal needs to review specifics.

Also: for customer audits we can provision redacted evidence to the secure drop (SOC2 controls mapping, network diagrams, key rotation records).

Rafael
